situation: Never chosen
given: a Staff Member whose Today has a desk section and who has never opened the switcher
then: the timeline is drawn

situation: A value that is not a layout
given: the cookie holds an old, empty or hand-edited value
then: the default is drawn, never an error and never a blank page

situation: Whose choice it is
given: two Staff Members share a desk PC
then: each keeps their own: the cookie is named for the Staff Member, so one person's choice never becomes the next person's

situation: Choosing is cosmetic
given: a Staff Member chooses another layout
then: the same summary is redrawn: nothing is read again, nothing is written at the Property, and what they may see or do is unchanged

situation: A role with no desk section
given: a Staff Member whose focus is housekeeping or finance
then: the overview is drawn and no switcher is offered: they lead with their own work, and a map of Guests is not theirs to see

situation: The overview stays
given: a Staff Member who prefers the cards
then: the page is drawn exactly as before this feature

situation: The desk section could not be read
given: any read it is made of failed
then: the layout says the section could not be read and offers a retry; the switcher still offers the overview; it is never drawn from the reads that did answer, because a map missing rooms looks like a smaller house

situation: A refresh fails
given: a desk layout is on screen with a good copy
then: the last good desk stays, marked stale, once; a second failure says it could not be read

situation: Every language
given: a Staff Member whose language is Turkish, English or Arabic
then: every string is in that language and none is missing; Arabic mirrors because positions are logical offsets, never left or right

situation: The night desk's surface
given: a Staff Member chooses the night desk
then: a dark surface scoped to that one layout, with the theme's own tokens re-pointed; this departs from docs/design/visual-reference.md, which names a single light palette, and needs the owner's decision

situation: Who it is built for
given: a Property whose front desk is switched on
then: only a front-desk or manager focus is given it, and only when the housekeeping board could be read

situation: An arrival is placed by its expected time
given: an arrival with an expected time inside the window
then: it sits where that time is on the line, and the present is marked on the same line; the line is drawn only when some arrival has a time (TL-S2-30)

situation: An arrival with no expected time
given: an arrival whose booking carries no time
then: it is a row in Still to arrive like every other arrival (TL-S2-29), saying it has no expected time, and is last in the plan; nothing is guessed and no list of names is left under the line

situation: A late arrival
given: an arrival whose time has passed and who is not in
then: an overrun is drawn back to when they were due and says how long, in the language's own hours and minutes, counted across midnight when the time was the day before's, so an arrival expected at 13:00 and read at 03:00 is 14 hours late and never 0 minutes; the plan ranks them above rooms at risk

situation: Check-in is offered wherever the viewer may and the booking is not blocked
given: an arrival whose room is awaiting inspection or dirty, and one whose room is blocked or out of service or whose booking is not confirmed
when: the row is drawn on any layout
then: the first offers Check in with the room's state beside it; pressing it asks in place "This room isn't ready yet" with Check in anyway, the same on the timeline, the house map and next up (TODAY-09), and the command still asks the server; the second offers no check-in, says why in words and links to the screen that mends it (housekeeping, departures or arrivals)

situation: The window
given: arrivals outside the next five hours
then: they are counted, not drawn, and one press shows the whole day

situation: A room with a guest in it is never ready, dirty or awaiting inspection
given: a room housekeeping calls ready, dirty or clean-awaiting-inspection that has a guest in house
then: it is in house and in none of the three; the figures and the board narrowed by ?show= count only empty rooms, so each number is the length of the list it opens (TODAY-03); the Rooms card's headline counts the vacant rooms and says so (TODAY-04)

situation: Another room for the guest
given: an arrival whose room is not ready
when: they are chosen on the map
then: ready rooms of the same type, not booked for another arrival today, say they can take them; the rest step back

situation: The map filters by state
given: a filter is chosen
then: only the rooms in that state are lit and the count on the filter is the rooms shown

situation: What to do first
given: several things are waiting
when: the plan or the queue is drawn
then: next up ranks a guest past their day to leave, then the one waiting longest to arrive, then the room at risk for the soonest arrival, then an arrival with no time; the timeline's plan leaves the overdue guests to the due-out list above it, where each has a Check out (TL-S2-31)

situation: Nothing is waiting
given: no departure is overdue and no arrival late, at risk or without a time
when: the plan or the queue is drawn
then: it says nothing is waiting, never an empty box

situation: One number for tonight
given: a day with arrivals and departures still to come, and a guest overdue to leave
when: the night desk, the timeline and the occupancy card are drawn
then: the waterfall ends at in house, less those still leaving, plus those still arriving: the occupancy card's own sum (TODAY-01), unclamped so a house booked past its rooms says so; the timeline's In house tile says N expected tonight of M rooms and that overdue guests are counted as staying until checked out (TODAY-01)

situation: Days waiting to close
given: a Staff Member at a Property the front desk reaches
then: the number waiting and the oldest are shown with a way to close them; none waiting says every day is closed; a failed read says nothing rather than zero

situation: The hand-over lists only what exists
given: nothing is outstanding
then: it says there is nothing to hand over

situation: Overdue before the day it is due
given: a guest whose day to leave was a day or more ago
when: the timeline or the queue is drawn
then: the timeline names the date it was due and next up says how many days late it is; neither invents a time of day it does not have

situation: Money only for those who may see it
given: a viewer without finance.manage_folio
then: no balance and no Folio id is in it; a viewer who holds it sees what each guest owes

situation: The desk section carries every row
given: more arrivals today than the cards list
then: every arrival is in it with its expected time; the card beside it keeps its own cap

situation: The desk section is whole or not at all
given: one of arrivals, departures, departed today, the board or who is in house failed
then: it is unavailable; a failed close-the-day read costs only that part

situation: Who is in a room
given: a room with a guest in house
then: it names them from the in-house read and when they leave; a bed is found in its room

situation: Overdue departures lead
given: an overdue departure and others due today
then: the overdue one is first

situation: The right clock
given: a Property in another zone from the machine
when: the present is placed on the line
then: it is the Property's own minutes since midnight, and midnight is zero

situation: A long due-out list folds
given: more departures are due than fit at a glance
then: the six most urgent are shown, overdue first, with a line that still counts every overdue guest and those leaving today; one press shows the rest and another folds them

situation: An open due-out list is grouped
given: a due-out list with overdue guests and others leaving today
then: the guests are grouped as overdue and leaving today, each with its count; a list of one kind has no group heading, since the line above it already says so

situation: A short due-out list
given: six departures or fewer
then: every one is shown and there is nothing to open

situation: What a departing guest owes
given: a viewer holding finance.manage_folio and a guest who owes
then: the amount is beside the name and the line above the list totals what is owed; a viewer without it sees neither, and a total of nothing is never drawn as nobody owing

situation: A long plan folds
given: more is waiting than fits at a glance
then: the five most urgent are shown in their ranked order and one press shows the rest, saying how many; the order never changes

situation: An open plan is grouped by kind
given: a plan with more than one kind of thing waiting
then: each kind has its own heading and count, in the plan's own order (next up: overdue departures first; the timeline's plan leaves them to the due-out list), and the numbers keep running through them

situation: A short plan
given: five things waiting or fewer
then: every one is shown and there is nothing to open

situation: One way in per row
given: a row the viewer can settle from the plan and one they cannot
then: the first has its command and no link; the second has the link to the screen that does, so no row is left without a way in

situation: A departure has no time of day
given: a stay with a day to leave and no hour
then: departures are listed above the line, not on it, because nothing says when in the day they are due; placing them needs a Property check-out time or one on the stay

situation: Guest requests on the hand-over
given: open requests at the Property
then: they are not listed; Today has no read of them and the Guest Experience page does (GX-12)

situation: A Property without housekeeping
given: a Property whose front desk is on and housekeeping is not
then: the overview, since the desk layouts need the board to say what a room is

situation: The choice follows the person across devices
given: a Staff Member who works at two desks
then: the other does not know; a cookie is per device, and following the person needs a preference record with its own migration and policy

situation: A room let by the bed
given: a room with several beds and several guests
then: one guest's name stands for the room

situation: Upcoming nights only for a manager
given: a front-desk focus that is not a manager
then: the next seven nights are not shown: booked ahead is the manager's depth (TD-S3-04)

situation: Entering the night desk by the hour
given: evening at the Property
then: still the person's choice; switching by hour is a product decision, since it needs an hour and a say per Property

situation: The switcher says what each layout is for
given: a Staff Member with a desk section opens the switcher
then: each layout says what it is for (the timeline: arrivals, departures and rooms across the day; next up: the most urgent job, one at a time; and so on) and one line says the choice is saved on this device (TODAY-23)

situation: Every arrival still to come is a row
given: arrivals still to come, with or without an expected time, in rooms that are ready or not
then: each is a row above the line in Still to arrive: room, guest, expected time or "no expected time", and Check in where the viewer may or the reason and a link where not; the list folds at six and counts the rest (TODAY-07, TODAY-08)
test_name: today-audit-fixes.spec.ts: every arrival still to come is a row with its command or its reason (TODAY-07, 08, 09)

situation: No line without a time
given: no arrival has an expected time, or some do
then: with none there is no chart, no range toggle and no legend; with some the axis keeps every hour label legible, the Now marker above the labels rather than on the first one (TODAY-22)

situation: An overdue guest appears once
given: a guest overdue to leave, with a Check out on the due-out list
then: the guest is one row with one Check out in the due-out list, and the plan beside it does not list them again but says the departures are listed above (TODAY-11)
test_name: today-audit-fixes.spec.ts: a Guest overdue to leave is one row with one Check out, and the plan says where they are (TODAY-11)

situation: Checked out is of the guests due today
given: guests checked out today, some due today still here, some overdue
then: checked out reads gone of gone plus leaving today, with the overdue guests counted apart in the line under it, so the denominator is the Overview's (TODAY-02)

situation: The hand-over names who is overdue
given: guests overdue to leave when the night desk is drawn
then: it says how many are overdue, names the one who has waited longest with room and days, adds what they owe for a viewer who may see money, and links to Departures (TODAY-10)

situation: Nights and days that do not fit
given: more days waiting to be closed than the card draws, and seven nights in a narrow card
when: the night desk or the timeline is drawn
then: the card says how many more days exist (+N) and each of the seven nights is a column that cannot run past its card, labelled by a short weekday and the day of the month (TODAY-16, TODAY-24)

situation: A long queue folds in next up
given: more is waiting than fits at a glance
then: the queue shows the five most urgent, keeps the chosen row visible, says how many are left and folds back; the arrows sit beside the title (TODAY-14)

situation: A tile says who and what
given: a room tile on the house map
when: it is read by a screen reader or a pointer
then: its name carries the room, the guest, what is happening and the room's state, and the guest's whole name is kept for a pointer; a blocked arrival says why and offers no check-in (TODAY-15)

situation: A phone
given: the timeline at a viewport below md
then: the due-out list and the arrivals lead and the four figures are compact, so the first screen is work and not four large numbers; nothing scrolls sideways (TODAY-21; the page title in the header bar and the bottom dock covering the last row belong to the shell)
test_name: today-audit-fixes.spec.ts: on a phone the due-out list leads and nothing scrolls sideways (TODAY-21)

situation: The first paint has the buttons
given: a viewer who may check guests out, opening Today
then: the Check out buttons are already in it, because the departures the dialog reviews are read with the summary and handed to the page, not fetched after it loads (TODAY-20)
test_name: today-audit-fixes.spec.ts: the first HTML already has the Check out buttons (TODAY-20)

situation: Check out many overdue guests at once
given: a long list of overdue guests, each with a balance or none
when: the desk wants to clear them
then: proposed, not built: select several and review one combined bill list before one confirm, with each balance and its reason still asked where the single dialog asks (TODAY-12; Mews and Opera Cloud both offer a multi-select check-out); until it is approved each guest is their own dialog

situation: A manager lands on the overview
given: a Manager or Owner opening Today with no saved choice
then: proposed, not built: the overview is drawn by default for them and the timeline stays the default for a desk focus; a saved choice still wins, and following the person across devices waits for TL-DEF-04 (TODAY-19; Apaleo and Cloudbeds open a manager on a property overview, a desk on arrivals)

situation: Recent activity names a person as the greeting does
given: an audit record whose actor has a display name
then: open: the row would show the display name the greeting and the account menu use; the users table has no display name and AL-S1-10 names actors by address, so this needs the owner's decision and a column before any code (TODAY-18)
